text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were slightly higher in late trade but off the session lows, weighed on by a drop in the dollar and narrow losses in U.S. debt markets. The June Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.97, up 0/29 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts shed some of their morning gains to end the sessionmodestly higher, volumes were very light after turbulent week, with fundamentals remained strong but market would carefully eye March 26 gilt auction. The June long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109-07/32, up 09/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures ended the week in cautious mood as traders continued to debate whether a U.S. interest rate rise next week, now widely expected, would be cause much damage at the long end of the yield curve. The June notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.84, up 0.52 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian debt markets lost their buoyancy at the last moment as dollar loses some strength and some BTP profit-taking set in. The June bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.14, up 0.03 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasury prices opened higher in line with overseas trends. Treasury prices gained in overseas trade and European government debt markets also displayed a firmer tone, analysts said curve-flattening trades were the order of the day. The June Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 108-22/32, up 01/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.96 percent.

JAPAN - Key June Japanese government bond (JGB) futures ended the Tokyo session sharply down on investors' selling of cash JGBs. In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 125.46, down 0.24 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - New issues business slowed sharply and was expected to remain light early next week ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting on Tuesday, when interest rates may be raised. Russia's Sverdlovsk region announced plans for a $100 million Eurobond. regional governor Eduard Rossel said it expected to be rated by Standard & Poor's within two months.
